clauses.reason: Terminated by statute on June 14, 1935. The sole operative command approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry under title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act ('do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry.'); the introductory recital and the five numbered findings command nothing. Actor: Congress, S.J. Res. 113, section 2, approved June 14, 1935. Legal basis for the first end. An approval of a code under section 3 of title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act had legal effect only through section 3: under 3(b) the code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade or industry and a violation in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce was an unfair method of competition under the Federal Trade Commission Act, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations and district attorneys were directed to sue, and under 3(f) each violation was a misdemeanor (the section 3 excerpt held in this packet). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935 (49 Stat. 375), repealed 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes' and states no effective date other than its approval. That repeal removed the power the approval rested on and every provision through which the approved code was enforced, which is the reason (not a default date) that it ends the prospective operative effect of this command on June 14, 1935. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, 295 U.S. 495 (decided May 27, 1935), held the section 3 code-making delegation unconstitutional ('we hold the code provisions here in question to be invalid'); the held excerpts record that as a validity characterization (an approval under an unconstitutional delegation was void from issuance under the doctrine then prevailing, and May 27, 1935 is when that was declared), not as an end date, because the judgment cancelled no other approving order and a later doctrine treats a measure's earlier existence as an operative fact. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of the resolution replaced the two-year expiry in section 2(c) with April 1, 1936, and nothing in the resolution defers section 2. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended before June 14, 1935; EO 6900 and EO 7020 amend the code and are later events, not ends.

research_rationale:
EO 6539-A (December 27, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt) approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry under title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The held text has an introductory 'Whereas' paragraph (the Secretary of Agriculture's submission, report, recommendations and findings), a findings paragraph with five numbered findings (application, notice and hearings, compliance with section 3(a) clauses (1) and (2), and tendency to effectuate the policy of section 1), and one operative paragraph ending 'do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry.' The machine inventory lists the five numbered findings as five clauses (the fifth span also swallows the operative paragraph and the signature line); findings command nothing, so I replaced it with one clause, characters 1402 to 1676, the operative approval sentence (inventory correction recorded). savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code before June 14, 1935 are completed (accrued) effects of the approval; the general savings statute of the time, which ordinarily preserves liabilities incurred under a repealed statute, is not a held source, and the repeal text contains no savings clause. Section 5 of title I exempted from the antitrust laws any code approved and in effect under the title and any action complying with it taken during the period; the resolution's proviso limits that exemption to agreements and action thereunder of two stated kinds and states no time limit, so the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action taken under codes before June 14, 1935. Whatever exemption or liability survives for past action is an accrued effect of completed acts, not continued operation of this approval. No held source shows a prosecution, injunction or other proceeding under this code continuing after June 14, 1935, and nothing continues the approval itself.
